title: Marked strictification of a semistable curve model
statement: Let $K$ be a separably closed field [def-weil-field, def-kun-separably-closed], and let $V\subseteq K$ be a valuation ring with fraction field $K$: for each $a\in K^\times$, either $a$ or $a^{-1}$ lies in $V$. Suppose the prime ideals of $V$ form a finite chain. Put $S=\operatorname{Spec}V$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum] and $\eta=\operatorname{Spec}K$. Let $(Y,E)$ be a semistable multipointed $S$-curve whose generic curve is smooth and whose generic marking is etale. There is a strictly semistable multipointed $S$-curve $(Z,F)$ and an $\eta$-modification of pairs $(Z,F)\to(Y,E)$ inducing the identity on the generic pair. Strict semistability means that Zariski locally on the curve and base the pair admits an etale morphism of pairs to either $(\operatorname{Spec}A[t],\{t=0\})$ or $(\operatorname{Spec}A[u,v]/(uv-a),\varnothing)$, where $a\in A$ and both maps on the curve and marking are etale; it implies semistability. A multipointed curve $(X,D)$ over a scheme $T$ means flat [def-weil-flat-morphism] finitely presented [def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation] morphisms $X\to T$, $D\to T$ of pure relative dimensions $1$, $0$ and a closed immersion $D\hookrightarrow X$ [def-weil-closed-immersion]; $D$ may be empty and $X$ need not be separated or proper over $T$. It is semistable if every singular point of every geometric fibre has completed local ring $\Omega[[u,v]]/(uv)$ over its algebraically closed residue field, $D\to T$ is etale [def-weil-etale-morphism], and $D$ lies in the relative smooth locus [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms]. For integral $T$ with generic point $\eta$, an $\eta$-modification of multipointed curves is a compatible pair $f_X:X'\to X$, $f_D:D'\to D$ of proper morphisms [def-weil-proper-morphism], each an isomorphism over a schematically dense open and on its generic fibre. A semistable such modification is stable if in each geometric fibre there is no irreducible component isomorphic to $\mathbf P^1$ that is contracted by $f_X$ and meets the union of the marking and the singular points of $X'$ in at most two points. Geometric fibres are [def-weil-geometric-fibre]; dimension is topological Krull dimension [def-kun-topological-krull-dimension]; the local completion is at the maximal ideal [def-weil-pbc-adic-completion], and $\Omega[[u,v]]$ denotes the two-variable formal power series ring [def-weil-pbc-multivariate-power-series]. Here an open immersion $j:U\hookrightarrow Z$ is schematically dense when $\mathcal O_Z\to j_*\mathcal O_U$ is injective.

proof.text: Let $N=\operatorname{Sing}(Y/S)$ be the first-Fitting singular subscheme. By [lem-trf-nodal-family-fitting-singular], its support is precisely the nonsmooth locus, is closed, and $N\to S$ is unramified. Apply the same node to each fibre $Y_s$: its singular subscheme is $N_s$ and is unramified over $\kappa(s)$. By [lem-weil-pbc-unramified-over-field-discrete], $N_s$ is discrete. It is quasi-compact, since it is closed in the finite-type $\kappa(s)$-scheme $Y_s$, so has finitely many points. There are finitely many $s\in S$, hence $|N|$ is finite. The same argument applies to every intermediate semistable $S$-curve below. For such a curve $X$, let $d(X)$ be the number of points of its nonsmooth locus at which at least one reduced component of the fibre through that point is not smooth over its residue field. This is a finite nonnegative integer.

source.place: Remark 4.5.2: agent reconstruction for the already semistable input; finiteness from Stacks 0C59, 0C5B and 02G7.

proof.text: Suppose $d(X)>0$ for the current semistable model $X$, and choose one point $z$ counted by $d(X)$. Apply [lem-trf-valuation-symmetric-nodal-blowup] to $X$ and $z$. It supplies $C=\overline{\{z\}}$, a global nonzero $\pi$ whose base vanishing set is the closure of $z|_S$, a neighbourhood $W$ of all of $C$, and the specified ideal $I$: it is $\operatorname{Fit}_1(\Omega^1_{X/S})+(\pi)$ on $W$ and the unit ideal off $C$. On every etale nodal chart its pullback is $(u,v,\pi)$, with $\pi^2$ dividing the chart's nonzero thickness. The node supplies the three blowup algebras, properness and semistability of $q:X^+\to X$, and smoothness of every fibre component at every point mapping into $C$. The centre is disjoint from the marking, since $C$ lies in the closed nonsmooth locus; the marking is therefore unchanged.

source.place: Remark 4.5.2; agent reconstruction by the symmetric nodal blowup along the whole closure of a chosen node, using the chart calculations of §4.3.

proof.text: The local operation of Step 2 strictly decreases $d$. Indeed, over $C$ there are no points counted by $d(X^+)$, by the fibre-component assertion of [lem-trf-valuation-symmetric-nodal-blowup]. Off $C$, $q$ is an isomorphism, so it introduces no new bad fibre points there and the old counted points outside $C$ are in bijection with the new ones. Fibre components correspond locally under this isomorphism; their smoothness at a point is unchanged. At least the chosen $z$ is removed from the count. Thus $d(X^+)\le d(X)-1$. Induction on the initial finite integer $d(Y)$ terminates in a semistable marked pair $(Z,F)$ with $d(Z)=0$. Throughout the induction the marking is isomorphic to $E$, the generic map is the identity, and the curve maps are proper; [lem-weil-pbc-proper-fp-permanence] gives properness of the finite composite $b:Z\to Y$.

source.place: Remark 4.5.2: finite decreasing-defect induction. The local fibre-component assertion is a separate cited input, not strictness inferred from a single closed fibre.

proof.text: Every reduced irreducible component of every fibre of $Z$ is smooth: at a smooth point of the fibre this is automatic, and at a node it follows from $d(Z)=0$. Apply [lem-trf-valuation-smooth-branches-strict-chart] to $(Z,F)$, with its smooth generic curve and unchanged etale marking in the smooth locus. This gives, at every point of $Z$, precisely a Zariski open strict pair chart over an open of $S$. Hence $(Z,F)$ is strictly semistable. The hypothesis here concerns all fibres; smooth components in only the most special fibre would not suffice for this inference over a higher-rank valuation ring.

source.place: Remark 4.5.2 and the strict-pair definition in §4.3: application of the separately stated all-fibres relative chart criterion.

proof.text: The map of markings $F\to E$ is an isomorphism, hence proper; $b$ is proper by Step 3. Both maps are the identity on the generic pair. The generic fibre is schematically dense in each flat scheme over the domain $V$: on an affine, flatness gives torsion-freeness, so the map from its coordinate ring to its localization over $K$ is injective. Consequently the open on which $b$ is an isomorphism (it contains the generic fibre) is schematically dense in source and target. The same holds for the marking, which is flat and unchanged. Therefore $(Z,F)\to(Y,E)$ is an $\eta$-modification of pairs with the prescribed generic identity. This argument includes $d(Y)=0$, the empty marking and the empty curve.

source.place: Remark 4.5.2, final verification of the definition of eta-modification; affine torsion-freeness argument written out.

proof_origin.place: Remark 4.5.2, printed p. 33, with symmetric nodal blowups reconstructed from §4.3. Finite decreasing-defect induction on bad fibre nodes; the operation acts on the whole closure of each chosen node, and the chart criterion requires smooth components in every fibre. The earlier stable-overlap and unspecified pushout argument is replaced, not attributed to the source.
